Based on my research, here are the Nobel Prize laureates in Physics from 2019 to 2020:

## **2019 Nobel Prize in Physics**

The 2019 prize was awarded to **three laureates** in two categories:

### 1. **Phillip James Edwin "Jim" Peebles** (½ of the prize)
- **Research Field:** Physical Cosmology
- **Citation:** "For his theoretical discoveries in physical cosmology"
- **Key Contributions:**
  - Primordial nucleosynthesis (understanding how the first elements formed)
  - Dark matter research
  - Cosmic microwave background (CMB) radiation
  - Structure formation in the universe
  - Cosmic infrared background and recombination epoch
- **Background:** Canadian-American theoretical cosmologist, Professor emeritus at Princeton University

### 2. **Michel Mayor** and **Didier Queloz** (shared the other ½ of the prize)
- **Research Field:** Exoplanet Discovery / Observational Astronomy
- **Citation:** "For the discovery of an exoplanet orbiting a solar-type star"
- **Key Contributions:**
  - Discovered **51 Pegasi b** in 1995 - the first extrasolar planet orbiting a Sun-like star
  - Used the **radial velocity method** (Doppler effect) to detect the planet
  - Employed the **ELODIE spectrograph** at Haute-Provence Observatory
- **Impact:** Launched the "exoplanet revolution" in astrophysics
- **Background:** Both Swiss astronomers from the University of Geneva (Queloz was Mayor's doctoral student)

---

## **2020 Nobel Prize in Physics**

The 2020 prize was also shared among **three laureates**:

### 1. **Roger Penrose** (½ of the prize)
- **Research Field:** Theoretical Physics / General Relativity
- **Citation:** "For the discovery that black hole formation is a robust prediction of the general theory of relativity"
- **Key Contributions:**
  - Developed mathematical techniques proving black holes are a direct consequence of Einstein's theory
  - His 1965 work showed that massive star collapse inevitably forms black holes with singularities
  - Laid the foundation for modern black hole physics
- **Background:** British theoretical physicist born in 1931

### 2. **Reinhard Genzel** and **Andrea Ghez** (shared the other ½ of the prize)
- **Research Field:** Astrophysics / Infrared Astronomy
- **Citation:** "For the discovery of a supermassive compact object at the centre of our galaxy"
- **Key Contributions:**
  - Independently mapped the orbits of stars near the Milky Way's center
  - Used **adaptive optics** to achieve precise measurements
  - Provided observational proof of **Sagittarius A*** - a supermassive black hole (~4 million solar masses)
  - Tracked stellar motions over more than 25 years
- **Background:** 
  - Genzel: German astronomer at Max Planck Institute and UC Berkeley
  - Ghez: American astronomer at UCLA (the 4th woman to win the Nobel Prize in Physics)

---

## **Summary**

The **2019 prizes** focused on understanding our cosmic origins (Peebles' cosmology) and discovering that we're not alone (Mayor & Queloz's exoplanet discovery).

The **2020 prizes** focused on black holes - from Penrose's theoretical groundbreaking work proving their existence, to Genzel and Ghez's observational proof of a supermassive black hole at the center of our galaxy.

All these discoveries fundamentally changed our understanding of the universe and our place in it.

The [Nobel Prize in Physics](Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics") ([Swedish](Swedish_language "Swedish language"): *Nobelpriset i fysik*) is awarded annually by the [Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences](Royal_Swedish_Academy_of_Sciences "Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences") to scientists in the various fields of [physics](Physics "Physics"). It is one of the five [Nobel Prizes](Nobel_Prize "Nobel Prize") established by the 1895 [will](Will_and_testament "Will and testament") of [Alfred Nobel](Alfred_Nobel "Alfred Nobel") (who died in 1896), awarded for outstanding contributions in physics.[[1]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-1) As dictated by Nobel's will, the award is administered by the [Nobel Foundation](Nobel_Foundation "Nobel Foundation") and awarded by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.[[2]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-2) The award is presented in <Stockholm> at an annual ceremony on 10 December, the anniversary of Nobel's death.[[3]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-3) Each recipient receives a medal, a diploma and a monetary award prize that has varied throughout the years.[[4]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-4)

## Statistics

The Nobel Prize in Physics has been awarded to 221 individuals until 2022.[[5]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-5) The first prize in physics was awarded in 1901 to [Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen](Wilhelm_R%C3%B6ntgen "Wilhelm Röntgen"), of Germany, who received 150,782 [SEK](Swedish_krona "Swedish krona"). [John Bardeen](John_Bardeen "John Bardeen") is the only laureate to win the prize twice—in 1956 and 1972. [Marie Skłodowska-Curie](Marie_Sk%C5%82odowska-Curie "Marie Skłodowska-Curie") also won two Nobel Prizes, for physics in 1903 and chemistry in 1911.

[William Lawrence Bragg](Lawrence_Bragg "Lawrence Bragg") was the youngest Nobel laureate in physics; he won the prize in 1915 at the age of 25. He was also the youngest laureate for any Nobel prize until 2014 (when [Malala Yousafzai](Malala_Yousafzai "Malala Yousafzai") won the Nobel Peace Prize at age 17).[[6]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-6) The oldest Nobel Prize laureate in physics was [Arthur Ashkin](Arthur_Ashkin "Arthur Ashkin") who was 96 years old when he was awarded the prize in 2018.[[7]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-7)

Only four women have won the prize: Curie, [Maria Goeppert-Mayer](Maria_Goeppert-Mayer "Maria Goeppert-Mayer") (1963), [Donna Strickland](Donna_Strickland "Donna Strickland") (2018), and [Andrea Ghez](Andrea_Ghez "Andrea Ghez") (2020).[[8]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-8)

There have been six years for which the Nobel Prize in Physics was not awarded (1916, 1931, 1934, 1940–1942). There were also nine years for which the Nobel Prize in Physics was delayed for one year:

- The 1914 prize awarded to [Max von Laue](Max_von_Laue "Max von Laue") was announced only in November 1915.[[9]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-N1914-9)
- The Prize was not awarded in 1917, as the Nobel Committee for Physics decided that none of that year's nominations met the necessary criteria, but was awarded to [Charles Glover Barkla](Charles_Glover_Barkla "Charles Glover Barkla") in 1918 and counted as the 1917 prize.[[10]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-N1917-10)
- This precedent was followed for the 1918 prize awarded to [Max Planck](Max_Planck "Max Planck") in 1919,[[11]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-N1918-11)
- the 1921 prize awarded to [Albert Einstein](Albert_Einstein "Albert Einstein") in 1922,[[12]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-N1921-12)

- the 1943 prize awarded to [Otto Stern](Otto_Stern "Otto Stern") in 1944.[[17]](List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-N1943-17)

Based on my research, here is comprehensive information about the **2019 Nobel Prize in Physics** laureates and their research contributions:

## 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics Winners

The prize was awarded to **three laureates** who received recognition in two distinct categories:

### 1. **Phillip James Edwin "Jim" Peebles** (Canadian-American)
**Half of the prize** was awarded to him "**for his theoretical discoveries in physical cosmology**"

**Background:**
- Born: April 25, 1935, in Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada
- Nationality: Canadian-American
- Education: University of Manitoba (BS), Princeton University (MS, PhD)
- Institution: Albert Einstein Professor in Science (emeritus) at Princeton University

**Research Contributions:**
- Widely regarded as one of the world's leading theoretical cosmologists since 1970
- Made major theoretical contributions to:
  - **Primordial nucleosynthesis** (understanding how the first elements formed)
  - **Dark matter** research
  - **Cosmic microwave background (CMB)** radiation
  - **Structure formation** in the universe
  - **Cosmic infrared background**
  - **Recombination** epoch in cosmology

### 2. **Michel Mayor** (Swiss) and **Didier Queloz** (Swiss)
**They shared the other half** of the prize "**for the discovery of an exoplanet orbiting a solar-type star**"

---

**Michel Mayor:**
- Born: January 12, 1942, in Lausanne, Switzerland
- Education: University of Lausanne (MS), University of Geneva (PhD)
- Institution: Professor emeritus at the University of Geneva's Department of Astronomy

**Didier Queloz:**
- Born: February 23, 1966, Switzerland
- Education: University of Geneva (MSc, PhD) - doctoral student of Michel Mayor
- Institution: Jacksonian Professor of Natural Philosophy at the University of Cambridge; also professor at the University of Geneva

**Their Groundbreaking Discovery:**
- In **1995**, Mayor and Queloz discovered **51 Pegasi b**, the first extrasolar planet (exoplanet) orbiting a Sun-like star (51 Pegasi)
- The planet was a **Hot Jupiter** - a gas giant orbiting very close to its star
- Detection method: Measured small periodic changes in the star's **radial velocity** using the **Doppler effect**
- Used a new spectrograph instrument called **ELODIE**, installed at the Haute-Provence Observatory in France

**Impact of Their Discovery:**
- Launched the "exoplanet revolution" in astrophysics
- Opened up the search for planets beyond our solar system
- Resulted in "contributions to our understanding of the evolution of the universe and Earth's place in the cosmos"
- Changed our understanding of planetary system formation and the possibility of finding other worlds

## Summary of Research Fields

The 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics covered two major areas:

1. **Physical Cosmology** (Peebles): Understanding the large-scale structure and evolution of the universe through theoretical frameworks
2. **Exoplanet Discovery** (Mayor & Queloz): Observational astronomy, radial velocity measurements, and the discovery of worlds beyond our solar system

Both contributions fundamentally changed our understanding of our place in the universe - Peebles theoretically explaining the cosmos from its beginning, while Mayor and Queloz discovered that other planetary systems exist, making us less alone in the universe.

## 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics Laureates

### The Prize Split

The 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics was divided as follows:
- **One half** awarded to **Roger Penrose** for theoretical work
- **The other half** jointly awarded to **Reinhard Genzel** and **Andrea Ghez** for observational work

### Roger Penrose (Theoretical Contribution - 1/2 of Prize)

**Research Field:** Theoretical Physics, General Relativity

**Nobel Citation:** "For the discovery that black hole formation is a robust prediction of the general theory of relativity"

**Key Contributions:**
- Developed mathematical techniques and theorems proving that black holes are a direct consequence of Einstein's general theory of relativity
- His groundbreaking 1965 work showed that black holes are a robust feature of general relativity, not just mathematical curiosities
- Proved that when massive stars collapse under their own gravity, they inevitably form black holes with singularities (points of infinite density)
- This work laid the foundation for our modern understanding of black hole physics
- Known for many other contributions including Penrose tiling, twistor theory, spin networks, and the Penrose process

**Background:** Born August 8, 1931, in Colchester, England. Educated at University College London and St John's College, Cambridge.

### Reinhard Genzel & Andrea Ghez (Observational Contribution - 1/2 of Prize together)

**Research Field:** Astrophysics, Infrared/Submillimeter Astronomy

**Nobel Citation:** "For the discovery of a supermassive compact object at the centre of our galaxy"

#### Reinhard Genzel
**Background:** Born March 24, 1952, in Bad Homburg vor der Höhe, Germany
- Institutions: Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics, University of California, Berkeley
- Education: University of Freiburg, University of Bonn

**Research Contributions:**
- Pioneered infrared astronomy techniques to observe the galactic center
- Led teams that tracked the orbits of stars near the center of the Milky Way
- Used adaptive optics to improve telescope resolution, allowing precise measurements of stellar motions
- Provided evidence for a supermassive black hole (Sagittarius A*) with a mass of about 4 million times that of our Sun

#### Andrea Ghez
**Background:** Born June 16, 1965, in New York City
- Institution: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA)
- Education: MIT (BS), California Institute of Technology (MS, PhD)
- Note: Only the fourth woman to win the Nobel Prize in Physics

**Research Contributions:**
- Independently confirmed Genzel's findings with her own observations
- Pioneered the use of adaptive optics on the Keck Observatory in Hawaii
- Mapped the orbits of dozens of stars orbiting the galactic center over more than 25 years
- Her team's work provided independent confirmation of the existence of Sagittarius A*
- Her research showed that the most likely explanation for the observed stellar motions is a supermassive black hole

### Significance of Their Work

Together, these laureates revolutionized our understanding of black holes:
- **Penrose** provided the theoretical foundation proving black holes must exist
- **Genzel and Ghez** provided observational proof of a supermassive black hole at the center of our own galaxy

Their work confirmed one of the most extreme predictions of Einstein's general relativity and opened up a new field of research into supermassive black holes and their role in galaxy formation and evolution.
